**5B.8 Research Note**
Overall: **mixed, leaning negative on realized distribution.** Sharif’s 2024 economic program clearly included broad social protection and lower-cost adjustments, but the available evidence does **not** show a strong, durable pattern of gains being distributed fairly across regions, classes, genders, and groups. Poverty still rose, vulnerable groups remained exposed, and there is little direct evidence of region-specific or equality-driven redistribution.

**Positive**
- **Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility** — IMF, 2024-07-12 — https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff — Claim: the program explicitly included continued protection for vulnerable groups through BISP, alongside tax-base broadening and SOE reform. This is the strongest evidence that the government aimed at some broad-based distribution rather than just elite gain. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

- **Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement** — IMF, 2024-05-10 — https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741 — Claim: the IMF said sustainable recovery required continued social protection, better tax collection, and structural reform. This supports a fairness-through-safety-net reading, though it is still program intent rather than proof of equal outcomes. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

- **Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says** — Reuters via Dawn, 2024-10-10 — https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298 — Claim: the government renegotiated power-purchase contracts to cut tariffs and save about Rs60 billion annually. Lower energy costs are a broad benefit that can reach households and firms across classes and regions, not just regime supporters. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`.

- **On National Minority Day, Sharif said minorities play a significant role in Pakistan’s stability and prosperity** — Radio Pakistan, 2024-08-11 — https://www.radio.gov.pk/11-08-2024/pm-reassures-equal-opportunities-for-minorities — Claim: Sharif publicly said minorities’ rights were constitutionally guaranteed and the government would protect equal opportunity. This is positive for fair inclusion, but it is rhetorical and not evidence of durable redistribution. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.

- **Government says it enacted legislative measures for vulnerable groups** — Press Information Department, Pakistan, 2024-12-10 — https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/27376 — Claim: the government said it had enacted measures for vulnerable groups and strengthened commissions for women, children, human rights, and minorities. This is institutional positive evidence, though it does not prove that gains reached these groups evenly in practice. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.6`.

**Negative**
- **Pakistan: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction** — World Bank, 2024-10-10 — https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank — Claim: growth recovered, but poverty still increased and the government still needed reforms to subsidies, the tax system, and the state’s role in the economy. That is strong evidence against a claim that economic gains were already being fairly shared. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.3`, `5B.4`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility** — IMF, 2024-10-10 — https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152 — Claim: the IMF said Pakistan still had a narrow tax base, weak governance, an outsized state role, and a business environment that hindered investment. This suggests the distribution of economic gains remained structurally skewed and incomplete. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **End escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community** — Amnesty International, 2024-06-21 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ — Claim: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and blocking of Ahmadi rites. That is negative evidence that an excluded minority was not receiving fair treatment or economic-political inclusion. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan government intensifies crackdown on political dissent** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-10-09 — https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent — Claim: HRW reported mass arrests, roadblocks, and internet cuts against PTI protesters, including peaceful demonstrators. This cuts against fair distribution because opponents and their social base were treated coercively rather than as equal claimants on state gains. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`, `5B.6`.

- **Pakistan authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community** — Amnesty International, 2024-06-21 — https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/ — Claim: the same report also says district authorities used preventive detentions and provincial police acted extrajudicially. This is direct evidence against fair treatment across groups. QIDs: `5B.8`, `5B.5`.

**Search Gap**
- I found little direct 2024 evidence on **region-by-region spending outcomes**, **gender-specific distribution of economic gains**, or whether Sharif explicitly redirected benefits toward opposition areas versus supporter strongholds.
- The strongest positive evidence is about **social protection and lower tariffs**; the strongest negative evidence is about **poverty still rising** and **minority/opposition groups remaining exposed**.
